Our Belgian friend and member, Etienne Gailly, was 7th, running for the Belgian Army, and our Poly member, Dick Towndrow, 15th, running for the British Army team.

Dick Towndrow, making one of his rare appearances in our colours, was a good winner of the scratch race, followed by Vic Blowfield, who in his first attempt at cross-country racing, certainly surprised many by his forward running.
One of our best runners of the past, it is good to see Alf out again. Dick Towndrow has now joined us as a first claim member.
We also welcome as a first-claim member our old friend Dick Towndrow, who finished 14th in last year's English Senior championship, when representing the Polytechnic Harriers.

Coming to the scratch race, this was won by Vic Blowfield with Dick Towndrow second and Ted Stimpson third. To beat the half-hour over our course is quite good running, so it can be seen that Vic put in some really fast running, which should gain him many honours before the season is over.
Gosney of Eastleigh beat Olney the local "crack" in the individual race, but our lads packed well with Tom Clinton 4th, Dick Towndrow 5th, Ted Stimpson 6th and Frank Abberton 7th.

Dick Towndrow gained his first club championship award in being third, with a past-holder in Arthur Penny fourth, and Tom Clinton fifth. The next two positions were filled by two junior members in Martin Williamson and Mike Heard.

Dick Towndrow won the 15 miles road race promoted by the Wigmore Harriers, and Geoff Pearson and Con Abberton finished equal fifth. In the Finchley "20" Geoff Pearson was 17th in 2 hrs. 13 mins. 31 secs., quite a creditable effort.

With the help of Dick Towndrow, and such as Archie Bedford, Eddie Short, Mike Heard, “Ginger” Kennedy and Jack Brown, to mention only a few of our promising members plus the help of last season's stalwarts, I think we shall have yet another successful year over the country.
